clue.text: Officer who could get car crime initially confused with tip-off?

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of car, a C and tip-off are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of crime is used

parts.note: taken as written, without the hyphen

explanation.surface: A police officer gets a tip-off about car crime and is muddled by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the C of crime; that and the letters of car and tip-off are shuffled, as 'confused' says.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic cop is a police officer who deals with road users and motoring offences.

clue.text: It goes in and out, stirring up 28

indicators.note: stirring up means mixing, so the letters of the answer at 28 are rearranged

parts.note: the number points to the solution of 28 across, a word meaning knotted

explanation.surface: Something that moves back and forth and agitates another clue's answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference supplies a four-letter word meaning knotted, whose letters 'stirring up' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea comes in and goes out twice a day, a playful description of the ocean's rise and fall.

clue.text: Communication from one who should inherit (masculine), so it's said

indicators.note: so it's said tells us the words are spoken, and the spelling we enter is a different one

parts.note: one who should inherit is an heir, and masculine is male, giving heir male

explanation.surface: A letter from a male heir to an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'heir male' (a male heir) is identical to the word for overseas post sent by plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Post carried by aircraft is a form of communication, a letter or parcel sent overseas.

clue.text: Finn knees car drunkenly: it's a gift!

indicators.note: drunkenly suggests staggering about, so the letters of Finn, knees and car are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunk Finnish man bumps his knees on a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' scrambles FINN KNEES CAR. The gift is one of the three the Magi brought to the infant Jesus, alongside gold and myrrh.
explanation.definitionFit: The aromatic resin was one of the Wise Men's offerings, so it is a famous gift.

clue.text: They could make waves in the beauty business

definitions.text: They could make waves in the beauty business

parts.words: They could make waves in the beauty business
parts.note: making waves sounds like causing trouble, but here it means putting waves into hair, as hairdressers do

explanation.walkthrough: 'make waves' suggests troublemakers; these are hairdressers, British slang, or tongs that crimp hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairdressers, informally, curl and wave hair; the word also names curling tongs used in salons.

clue.text: 'A bird, otherwise?!' I yell in Spanish

parts.note: otherwise means or, as in 'come now, or else'
ole is the Spanish shout of approval heard at bullfights

explanation.surface: Someone shouts in Spanish, wondering if what they see is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden oriole is a bright yellow and black songbird, an example of a bird.

clue.text: From the east, serves in Lebanese cafe

indicators.note: from the east means reading right to left in an across clue, so the letters run backwards
in tells us the letters sit inside the words Lebanese cafe

explanation.surface: Something is served from the east in a Lebanese cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds SECA in lebaneSE CAfe, and 'From the east' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, unreturnable services are called aces, so the word works as a plural noun for serves.

clue.text: Not able to rest in peace, with Scottish witch's spell

parts.note: not able is can't, written without the apostrophe
rest in peace is abbreviated RIP on gravestones

explanation.surface: A Scottish witch casts a spell so the dead cannot rest in peace.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scots word means a magic charm or trick, particularly one used by a witch.

clue.text: Moves over and treads on assistant carrying son

parts.note: to tread is to step, so treads gives steps

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the assistant word has the son letter inside it

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: Someone treads on a helper who is holding a little boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts S inside AIDE to give ASIDE; 'on' just joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To make room by stepping out of the way is to move over, an idiomatic match.

clue.text: The German paint finish — it is giving you a skin complaint

parts.note: der is the German word for the (masculine)
a matt or mat finish is a non-glossy paint finish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A German paint with a particular finish gives someone a skin rash.
explanation.definitionFit: This condition is inflammation of the skin, a general medical term for a skin complaint.

clue.text: Old northern Conservative with ecstasy a while back

parts.note: C abbreviates Conservative, the British political party
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An elderly northern Tory admits to taking ecstasy years ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning formerly, at some time in the past, the word is a synonym for a while back.

clue.text: Brief exhalation of relief: 1950s troublemaker unable to see at a distance

definitions.text: unable to see at a distance

parts.note: brief means short
a sigh is a breath let out in relief
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress with a rowdy reputation

explanation.surface: A short sigh of relief from a 1950s delinquent with poor eyesight.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in drape jackets, seen as troublemakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia means distant objects are blurred, which is what the medical term for poor far vision describes.

clue.text: Hastily fasten bridle, etc

definitions.meaning: to fix something quickly and loosely, as with a small nail or long stitches
saddles, bridles and other riding gear, collectively called by the stable-yard term

explanation.surface: Someone hurriedly fixes a horse's bridle and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a quick temporary fastening and, short for tackle, horse-riding equipment.

clue.text: Fish and chips cooked with lard

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients being transformed, so the letters of chips and lard are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fish and chips fried in lard, the classic chip-shop meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' scrambles CHIPS with LARD.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small oily sea fish of the herring family, adult sardines.

clue.text: I detest established imagery: I study nothing about object personifying cobblers

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
O looks like zero, nothing
C is the abbreviation of circa, about
a last is the foot-shaped block a shoemaker works on, the very emblem of the trade

explanation.surface: A rebel declares a hatred of old images and mocks cobblers' tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cobblers' is also British slang for nonsense, adding to the scorn. 'The cobbler should stick to his last' is the proverb behind the object.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attacks cherished beliefs or images would say this of themselves, a definition in the first person.

clue.text: Concerning the kitchen Lucy and I ran badly

indicators.note: badly suggests things done wrong, so the letters of Lucy, I and ran are jumbled

explanation.surface: Lucy and the speaker ran a kitchen poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles LUCY, I and RAN together.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to cooking, so it means pertaining to the kitchen.

clue.text: It's curtains for the Yanks!

parts.note: it's curtains sounds like the end for Americans, but it means the American word for curtains

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's curtains' is the idiom for doom; here it is literal: Americans call curtains by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English heavy window curtains are known by this term, so it is curtains to Americans.

clue.text: Not well: provide care for abuse

parts.note: not well means ill
a doctor treats a patient, giving them care

explanation.surface: A sick person is given medical care.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle someone cruelly is to abuse them; the hyphenated verb is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Nitrogen associated with the clear upper air, or lower?

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
ether was the old name for the pure air of the upper heavens

explanation.surface: A question about nitrogen in the atmosphere, high or low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upper' in the wordplay is set against the definition 'lower' to mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic adjective means situated beneath, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: Working the land, up to a certain time in life

parts.note: till means up to, as in 'till noon'
an age is a particular point in someone's life

explanation.surface: Working the land until a certain age.
explanation.definitionFit: Ploughing and cultivating soil for crops is called this, so it is working the land.

clue.text: Stingy Edward shut in the cupboard

parts.note: close means mean with money
Ted is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A miserly man called Edward is locked in a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a cupboard, so being shut away in one, or in private, fits.

clue.text: Plant to mostly support firm

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the support word is used

parts.note: to back is to support
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A plant that should mostly support a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts BACK to BAC.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaves are smoked, but the name is first that of the nicotine-bearing plant.

clue.text: Spirit of place, in Switzerland?

definitions.meaning: an old name for gin, from the Dutch genever
the city on Lake Leman in western Switzerland

explanation.surface: Asking about the spirit of a Swiss town.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an archaic name for Dutch gin and also a famous Swiss city.

clue.text: Old 'tec was agitated: came out in this?

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of old, tec and was are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old detective was nervous and broke out in sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' scrambles OLD, TEC and WAS. 'Tec is short for detective. 'came out in this' completes the idiom 'came out in a cold sweat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear makes a person break into clammy perspiration, which one is said to come out in.

clue.text: Taunt European going after rock

indicators.note: going after means the European letter is placed behind the rock word

parts.note: the Rock is Gibraltar, informally Gib

explanation.surface: Mocking a European who climbs a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibraltar, a British territory, is called the Rock or Gib.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeer or mocking remark is a taunt, and this spelling is a common variant of jibe.

clue.text: Looks up and down

indicators.note: up and down means the word reads the same both ways in this down entry

parts.note: looks, as a verb, means observes or perceives with the eyes

explanation.surface: Someone looks a person up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up and down' says the letters are the same read upward or downward.
explanation.definitionFit: To see is to look or observe, so the third-person verb matches looks.

clue.text: A bad actor returning to be servant

indicators.note: returning means turning back, so the bad actor word is written backwards

parts.note: a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: A poor actor comes back to work as a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses HAM to MAH.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Asian word for a nursemaid or female domestic servant.

clue.text: Crete: place designed for a holdall?

indicators.note: designed means arranged anew, so the letters of Crete and place are rearranged

explanation.surface: A place on Crete built to hold everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' scrambles CRETE and PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A container holds things, so it is jokingly a hold-all; the question mark flags the literal reading.

clue.text: Occasionally, this journalist should get knotted!

indicators.note: occasionally means taking every other letter of the word this

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A mock order telling a journalist to get lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' picks the odd letters of 'this'. 'Get knotted' is British slang for go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tied with a knot is knotted, a straightforward past participle synonym.

clue.text: Easily disgusted? Don't eat fish before ten with us

parts.note: to fast is to go without food
the id, or ide, is a freshwater fish
IO looks like the figures 1 and 0, ten

explanation.surface: A picky person refuses to eat fish, avoiding dinner with others.
explanation.walkthrough: IO is the digits 1 and 0 read as letters, ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A fussy person who is hard to please is readily put off, so easily disgusted.
